paras: The Terrell gambling raid shooting took place on the night of April 27, 1882, when the city marshal of Terrell, Texas, fired three pistol shots at a man fleeing a raid on a "colored gambling den." The man escaped unhurt, and one arrest was made in the raid.

According to a Terrell special to the Dallas Herald dated April 28, the marshal raided "one of the colored gambling dens of the town" the night before. When the marshal ordered those inside to surrender, one of them knocked him down and ran. From the ground, the marshal fired three shots from his pistol after the fleeing man, who "escaped unhurt."

One person was arrested in the raid, though the dispatch did not say whether it was the man who had fled. No names were given, and no follow-up report of charges or of the man's capture appears in the coverage.

The Dallas Daily Herald printed the item on April 29 on its first page, as the second paragraph of a short Terrell column. The first paragraph of that column reported that four Black men had been arrested for breaking into a grocery store on Virginia Street, so the raid appeared as one more piece of local crime news. The dispatch gave the marshal's account without comment, describing the den only as "colored" and calling the officer the "fallen officer" after he was knocked down. No other paper is known to have carried the story.
